summary: Backend-only test of the new instructor→follower push-notification ledger. 7/7 pytest cases pass covering class fan-out, past-date silence, event fan-out on create, draft→publish flip, PATCH idempotency, past-event silence, non-follower isolation, and the unique-index duplicate-key guard. Ledger rows land under (user_id, entity_type, entity_id); the send_push relay logs warnings in preview (expected, unrelated to correctness).

minor.issue: Past-dated events are silenced only for push fan-out (correct) — but the event itself is still persisted. If product intent is to reject past-dated events entirely, add a 400 validator. Currently by design so noting as minor.

action_items: None — feature works as specified. Optional: consider rejecting past-dated event/class POSTs at validation time if that matches product intent.
critical_code_review_comments: services/instructor_notifications.py::notify_followers_of_new_class silences past classes via string compare on ISO date — relies on class_doc['date'] being 'YYYY-MM-DD'. ClassSessionIn enforces the format only implicitly (string field); a client posting 'today' or 'Jan 5' would bypass the past-date check. Consider a Pydantic validator on ClassSessionIn.date.

notify_followers_of_new_event checks event_doc.get('is_published', True) — defaults to True when the key is missing. events_svc.create_event always sets is_published explicitly so it's fine today, but if a future code path forgets it, drafts will notify. Prefer explicit False default.
PATCH /api/events publish-flip logic reads existing.is_published defaulting to False and out.is_published defaulting to True — same asymmetry. Works with current create_event but is fragile.
_follower_ids projects user_id only; a follower whose user_id field is missing is silently skipped. Fine, but no logging so an operator can't tell if a follower list looks smaller than expected.
seed_data_creation: Two throwaway dancer accounts (email prefix TEST_dancer_*), 4 test classes, 3 test events, and the corresponding instructor_notifications rows were created during the run. All were deleted in the module-scoped cleanup fixture — verified 0 leftover TEST_* users, classes, events, or ledger rows in Mongo after the run.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file /app/backend/tests/test_instructor_notifications.py covers the full ledger fan-out contract. Reusable — safe to run standalone (`pytest tests/test_instructor_notifications.py`). It reads EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env and MONGO_URL/DB_NAME from /app/backend/.env directly (no env-sourcing needed). Assumes Erin (erinboroughs@gmail.com / <redacted-SEC-001>) is seeded and there is at least one dance in db.dances. Push relay warnings in backend logs during the run are expected (Emergent Push not wired in preview).
rca_of_issue: N/A — no regression. Implementation matches spec: hooks fire from POST /api/classes and POST /api/events plus the draft→publish flip inside PATCH /api/events/{id}; the (user_id, entity_type, entity_id) unique index prevents duplicate rows; past-dated content is silenced via cheap ISO string compare against today; excluded self-notification of the posting instructor works because _follower_ids removes the instructor_id from the follower set.
